# [[1.0.0 P-30]] LFM2.5-8B-A1B — Hybrid MoE Edge Model from Liquid AI

**Authors**: Liquid AI (model card, engineering team)
**Year**: 2026
**Venue**: Hugging Face model card + Liquid AI engineering blog + Ollama library listing
**eprint / DOI**: arXiv:2511.23404 (model card); no formal academic publication
**Cited by**: [[primitives/INDEX]] entries [[PRIM-31]] (Iterative Retrieval Refinement — local-model context-window anchor), [[PRIM-29]] (Recruitment-Adaptive Planning — edge-tier roster entry)

## Summary

[[Liquid-2026-LFM2.5]] is Liquid AI's 2026 release of a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model sized for on-device inference. Total parameter count is ~8B with ~1B active per token ("A1B"), organised as a hybrid (sparse-MoE + dense) backbone trained with Liquid's STAR topology-search objective. Key engineering claims: 128K-token context window in the default variant; sub-100ms first-token latency on Apple Silicon and recent Snapdragon X-class CPUs when quantised to 4-bit (MLX-8bit variant listed on Hugging Face); bandwidth-adaptive expert routing so that the number of activated experts falls when memory pressure rises. The model card documents benchmark numbers (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, MultiPL-E) that place it between Phi-3.5-mini and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, with a notable edge advantage on long-context retrieval. For local coding agents it is one of the first open MoE models that can run an entire [[PRIM-23]] chunked-translator loop on a laptop without offloading experts.

## Relevance to MAgHARCM

LFM2.5-8B-A1B is one of two flagship "edge-tier" entries in MAgHARCM's [[PRIM-29]] recruitment roster (the other being Phi-3.5-mini), and the LFM2.5 model card is the empirical justification for [[PRIM-31]] Iterative Retrieval Refinement's design. Because LFM2.5 can hold a 128K context window even on CPU-only inference, the [[PRIM-26]] Navigator's per-iteration re-index of prior translated fragments can fit an entire chunked-translation history into a single prompt at iteration i+1 — the tight-window claim of [[PRIM-31]] is bounded by the model-card number, not by speculation. The hybrid MoE routing also explains why MAgHARCM's recruitment can downsize from a 30B reasoning tier to an 8B edge tier mid-loop when validator feedback indicates the fragment is mechanical (idiom mapping, type coercion) rather than semantic (control-flow restructuring). LFM2.5 is therefore both a concrete roster entry and the empirical ceiling for what the local-recruitment primitive can promise.

## Hop-1 References

- [[Mixtral-2024]] — the original open MoE baseline that LFM2.5 inherits the A×B naming convention from (Mixtral 8×7B); architectural ancestor.
- [[Phi-3-2024]] — the small-model peer in MAgHARCM's recruitment roster; Phi-3-mini and LFM2.5 trade off pure-quality vs. context-length.
- [[DeepSeek-MoE-2024]] — fine-grained expert segmentation + shared-expert isolation; the architectural pattern LFM2.5's hybrid-MoE design extends.
- [[Qwen3-MoE-2025]] — dense + MoE family with thinking-mode toggle; another current open MoE in the same recruitment tier.
- [[GLM-Family-2024-2026]] — Chinese open MoE lineage (ChatGLM → GLM-4.5/GLM-5); another MoE roster entry.

## Hop-2 Anchors (software-archaeology lean)

- [[Foltz-2023]] — DR.JONES cognitive model predicts that linear-traversal comprehension saturates quickly; LFM2.5's edge advantage on long-context retrieval is the empirical confirmation that motivates [[PRIM-31]]'s "tighter context window" claim rather than a "larger context window" claim.
- [[Muller-2022]] — legacy modernization case studies predate MoE; they implicitly assume a single-model setting, which is why MAgHARCM's [[PRIM-29]] recruitment step is novel — there is no Muller-era precedent for swapping models mid-pipeline.
- [[Baldwin-Clark-2000]] — design-rule decomposition predicts that sub-components (the "experts" in MoE terminology) should have stable interfaces (L1) and be substitutable leaves (L3); LFM2.5's expert routing is the practical proof that this decomposition is also how neural modules want to be organised.
